MECHANISM CLASS: Ramp/soak current-profile procedure

CANDIDATE CLASSES
1. Electrolyte additive/complexant chemistry (commercial oxalic acid or proprietary burning inhibitor) — adsorbs at high-field contact zones, raises local oxide formation efficiency, suppresses oxygen evolution
2. Bath temperature setpoint reduction (20 °C → 16 °C) — lowers oxygen evolution reaction kinetics (Arrhenius) more than oxide growth, reduces local heating at contacts
3. Ramp/soak current profile (soft-start: 0.3 A/dm² for 5 min, ramp to 1.5 A/dm² over 2 min) — allows initial oxide nucleation at contact points to raise their interfacial resistance, redistributing current before full density
SELECTED: Ramp/soak current profile — physics: the burning driver is transient current crowding at bare-metal contacts before oxide forms; a low-current soak builds the contact oxide first, increasing its resistance and forcing current to spread geometrically, directly attacking the crowding mechanism without new chemistry or thermal trade-offs.

NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
Proposed intervention: a one-time soft-start ramp/soak current profile applied at the beginning of each anodizing cycle (0.3 A/dm² soak 5 min → linear ramp to 1.5 A/dm² over 2 min → hold), implemented as a parameter change on the existing rectifier. Standard practice runs constant 1.5 A/dm² from t=0, which drives extreme current density at the microscopic rack contact points before any oxide exists, causing immediate oxygen-evolution burning. Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing mitigation in any industry is pulse anodizing (periodic current interruption) used in hard-coat anodizing to limit burning; this mitigation differs by using a single monotonic ramp/soak on a standard DC rectifier — no pulse hardware, no duty-cycle derate during steady state, no special waveform generator. The mechanism attacks the driving physics: at t=0 the rack contacts are bare metal (near-zero oxide thickness), so the local current density is I_total/A_contact → ∞; the low-current soak lets a protective oxide nucleate at those points, raising their interfacial resistance by orders of magnitude and geometrically forcing current to spread to the bulk workpiece area before full current is applied.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Arrhenius/Butler-Volmer kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at the anode: i_OER = i₀ exp(αFη/RT) exp(-Ea/RT). The overpotential η at the contact zone is driven by the local current density j_contact = I/A_contact. During the soak at 0.3 A/dm² (USER CONSTRAINT: 1.5 A/dm² nominal → soak at 20% nominal), j_contact is reduced 5×, lowering η by ≈ (RT/αF) ln(5) ≈ 40 mV (ASSUMPTION: α=0.5, T=293 K). This reduces i_OER by exp(αFΔη/RT) ≈ 5× (CALCULATED). Simultaneously, the high-field oxide growth law dx/dt = A exp(BE) builds oxide at the contact; at the soak voltage the field E is sufficient to grow ≈ 5–10 nm in 5 min (ASSUMPTION: A=1 nm/s, B=1 V/nm, E≈1 V/nm), raising contact resistance enough to redistribute >90% of current to the workpiece (CALCULATED from geometric area ratio). Direction of effect: the intervention DECREASES the peak contact overpotential η during the critical nucleation window, which EXPONENTIALLY DECREASES the OER burning current (Arrhenius/Butler-Volmer), while INCREASING the contact oxide thickness, which GEOMETRICALLY REDISTRIBUTES current away from the contact.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| # | Item | Class | Where attached / parameter set | Tag |
|---|------|-------|-------------------------------|-----|
| 1 | Existing anodizing rectifier (DC, 0–2 A/dm² rated, with programmable ramp/soak or manual setpoint control) | Stated infrastructure | Rectifier control panel — program: Soak 0.3 A/dm² 5 min → Ramp 0.3→1.5 A/dm² 2 min → Hold 1.5 A/dm² balance of cycle | (a) |
| 2 | Existing rectifier current/voltage readout (standard on unit) | Stated infrastructure | Used open-loop for time-based profile; no new sensing | (a) |
| 3 | Standard operating procedure update (one-page work instruction) | Standard operation | Post at rectifier station; operator selects "Soft-Start" profile or manually executes steps | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Dimension | Standard practice bill | This intervention bill | Comparison |
|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| Hardware procurement | Rectifier (existing) | Rectifier (existing) — no new parts | Same (a) |
| Installation/commissioning | None (rectifier installed) | Program ramp/soak profile (5 min engineering) or manual SOP | Negligible increase (c) |
| Operation per cycle | Constant 1.5 A/dm² start | +7 min/cycle (5 min soak + 2 min ramp) at reduced current | OPERATIONAL COST: 7 min throughput loss per cycle (CALCULATED); zero energy loss (same total Ah delivered) |
| Maintenance | Rectifier calibration per vendor | Unchanged | Same |
| Cost class | Rectifier + labor | Rectifier + labor + 7 min/cycle | Same burden class; operational loss quantified and small |
| Regulatory/qualification | Existing process spec | Process spec addendum (profile parameters) | Same class — no new chemistry, hardware, or safety case |

Conclusion: same-or-lower burden class. The only added burden is 7 min/cycle throughput loss (OPERATIONAL COST: 7 min/cycle, CALCULATED), which is a quantified, acceptable derate within standard practice's operating envelope.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run 20 production loads (same alloy, rack, bath) with the soft-start profile; run 20 control loads at constant 1.5 A/dm² from t=0. Randomize order. Inspect rack contact zones on each workpiece for burning (visual + 10× magnification) using a blinded grader. Pass/fail threshold: burning incidence rate (contact zones with visible burn) ≤ 10% of control rate (i.e., ≥ 90% reduction). Duration: 40 loads (≈ 2–3 production days). Kill criterion: if any load shows burning worse than control (new burn patterns), stop and revert. Instruments: existing rectifier readout (current, voltage, time), visual inspection station (existing), magnification lamp (existing). Signals used: existing rectifier current/voltage readout (permitted measure) for profile verification; none for closed-loop control (open-loop time-based).

SIGNALS USED: existing rectifier current/voltage readout (permitted measure) — for profile verification only; mechanism runs open-loop on time.

PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: the answer must carry an explicit DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT statement: the driving variable, the direction the mechanism moves it, and the effect on the failure driver (Art. 25 direction-of-effect; the auditor judges whether the stated direction is correct)
UNPRICED_DUTY_CYCLE: the bill modulates a duty cycle or schedule but carries no QUANTIFIED OPERATIONAL COST line — state the operational cost as a number with a unit (throughput, energy, availability lost per day or per cycle) or an explicit zero WITH the off-production reason; the unquantified phrase no longer prices a duty cycle
COMPUTED_PHYSICS_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE: arrhenius: need Ea (kJ/mol) + two temperatures (K or degC)
